newsitem.title: USA: Equitable to sell Lend Lease a unit.
newsitem.headline: Equitable to sell Lend Lease a unit.

text.p: The Equitable Cos Inc of the U.S. said on Thursday it signed a definitive agreement for Australia's Lend Lease Corp to buy its Equitable Real Estate Investment Management Inc unit for $400 million.

Lend Lease is an international property and financial services company based in Sydney and Equitable Real Estate is the U.S.'s largest manager of pension fund assets invested in real estate, the company said.
Lend Lease would pay Equitable $300 million in cash and $100 million in an eight-year note, Equitable said.

The new company formed by Lend Lease's acquisition of Equitable Real Estate would establish a global real estate company active on five continents with combined real estate assets under management of nearly $35 billion, including more than 60 investment funds, Equitable said.

The sale would include Equitable Real Estate's investment management business, two property management subsidiaries -- COMPASS Management and Leasing Inc, its mortgage unit COMPASS Retail Inc and ERE Rosen, a REIT management firm, it said.
The transaction was expected to close in the second quarter and was contingent on regulatory approval, it said.

"This transaction allows Equitable to realise the substantial equity built up in our successful real estate subsidiary over the years, and to retain its superior investment services on an ongoing basis to oversee our existing portfolios," Joseph Melone, president and chief executive officer of The Equitable Cos, said.
Melone said the sale was consistent with its strategy to reduce investment in real estate and concentrate on growing Equitable's core insurance and annuity businesses.
Equitable said Lend Lease would merge Equitable Real Estate with its U.S. real estate advisory firm Yarmouth Group. The new company would be called ERE/Yarmouth.

George Puskar, Equitable Real Estate's chairman, would serve as chairman and Matthew Banks, chief executive officer of Lend Lease Global Real Estate, will become chief executive officer of ERE/Yarmouth, the company said.
Under terms of the deal, ERE/Yarmouth would still serve as adviser for the real estate assets of Equitable Life's general account and for its real estate separate accounts.

Including $10 billion from Equitable's General Account, Equitable has $25 billion in assets under management and ranks as the largest U.S. manager of tax exempt real estate assets, as well as the country's third biggest property management firm. Its clients include 300 major U.S. corporate, public and union pension funds, and international investors, it said.
J.P. Morgan acted as exclusive adviser to The Equitable for this transaction.
Lend Lease first announced it entered talks with Equitable at the start of January.
